Anya: quick heads-up — seeing structured output drift on canary for quantized variants (AWQ / GPTQ int8). sample failures attached below.

Sam: repro steps? which model + quant backend?

Anya: model: redwood/long-dialogue-13b@v2.3. quant backends: awq-int8 and gptq-8bit. Canary config: batch_size=8, continuous_batching=true, kv_cache=true. Test harness: 5k synthetic funcall prompts from eval corpus.

Anya: failure example (one line returned as escaped string instead of JSON object):

```
{"tool_call": "{\"name\": \"payment_processor\", \"args\": \"{\\\"amount\\\": 99, \\\"currency\\\": \\\"USD\\\"}\"}"}
```

Anya: instead of the expected nested JSON object in args it becomes a double-escaped string. Sporadic: about ~2.4% of examples on AWQ-int8, ~0.9% on GPTQ-8bit, baseline float32 ~0.05%.

Lee Chen: could be tokenization + quoting behavior around braces. AWQ has slightly different softmax rounding earlier in the sequence so we end up emitting `\"` characters. Have we tried normalizing tokenizer output or running with raw logits to see where quotes appear?

Maria-G: also check continuous_batching — I’ve seen cases where prefix KV reuse mixes prompt boundaries and you get escaping because the model completes into the prior turn. Can you repro with batch_size=1 + no continuous_batching?

Anya: good call. I ran quick ablation:
- batch_size=8, continuous_batching=true -> schema failures 2.4%
- batch_size=1, continuous_batching=false -> schema failures 0.1%
- batch_size=1, continuous_batching=true -> 0.8%
So batching and KV both amplify it.

eval-bot: automated eval summary: AWQ-int8: 120/5000 invalid-struct outputs (2.4%), GPTQ-8bit: 45/5000 (0.9%), FP8-ish (fp8-compat): 12/5000 (0.24%), float32 baseline: 3/5000 (0.06%). Links: https://ci.redwood/evals/1851239999

Sam: nice numbers. Next steps: (1) can we reproduce locally single-threaded with a minimal prompt that triggers the escape? (2) bisect quant backend configs (awq packing params, group size) (3) run with tokenizer.debug=true and log tokens + emitted text.

Lee Chen: I can take (1) and (3) — will run with debug logits + tokenizer offsets. Any specific prompt that flares?

Anya: yes — the failing subset seems to have nested JSON in a single arg and unbalanced internal quotes: e.g. prompt ends with: `Please call payment_processor with args:` then model emits the JSON. I’ll paste a distilled repro in the thread in a sec.

Anya: distilled repro prompt: `Call tool as JSON: {"name":"payment_processor","args":{"amount":__AMOUNT__}}` with __AMOUNT__ replaced by values like 99, 0, 1000. AWQ tends to stringify when the numeric value distribution is skewed.

Maria-G: can we try a mitigation: force the tokenizer to insert explicit space before `{` or enforce single-turn generation by adding sentinel tokens? Might mask but could be a viable short-term deploy mitigation for Dedicated customers.

Sam: agree — mitigation path + root cause. Action items: Lee (repro + tokenizer logs), Anya (collect failing prompt IDs + example tokens), Maria (test sentinel-space mitigation on canary), Sam (coordinate quant-bakeoff runs across awq/gptq with group sizes).

Anya: assigning and will upload failing IDs to the eval board. thanks all. :thumbsup:
